description: Behavioural obligations for the §8.7.1 session-scoped drain — ownership, claim semantics, back-compat isolation, attestation, and the strip rule. Concurrency- and identity-critical; proven against a conformant Hub.
obligation: DRAIN OWNERSHIP (§8.7.1/§16.3): (1) `GET /v1/inbox?session=` MUST present the caller's OWN session: a foreign or unknown session -> 404 (indistinguishable, the §9.1 stance); the caller's own-but-TERMINAL session -> 410 — distinct by design, so a bridge returning from a lease lapse learns 're-register and continue' instead of treating its own address as nonexistent. The same rule governs `POST /v1/inbox/ack?session=` and the §8.8 `?session=` parameter. (2) Session presentation on an ack affects lease attribution ONLY, never ack authorization (which stays credential-scoped). SESSION-LESS ISOLATION (§8.7.1): (3) A session-less drain returns EXACTLY the v0.4 shape — a 0.4 consumer never sees a `message`/`response`/`receipt` entry (back-compat by construction); the v0.5 entry kinds are delivered ONLY to session-presenting drains. (4) The §8.7 webhook remains directives-only in v0.5 — no v0.5 entry kind is ever webhook-delivered. VISIBILITY + CLAIM (§8.7.1): (5) Session-addressed entries are visible only to drains presenting that session. (6) Principal-addressed entries are visible to any session-presenting drain of the destination principal, FIRST-CLAIM-WINS: under N concurrent session-presenting drains, exactly ONE receives a given entry per visibility window (a claimed entry is hidden until acked or the window lapses). (7) Crashed-claimant rescue: a claimant that dies mid-processing without acking is rescued by ordinary visibility-timeout redelivery to a sibling session — which is why the §14.2 bounce rules are scoped to session-addressed mail. ATTESTATION + STRIP (§8.7.1/§13.1): (8) A delivered `message` entry's `from` is Hub-attested, never request-supplied — `agent:<id>` or, when the submit carried `agent.session`, `agent:<id>#<sess>` carrying EXACTLY the submitted session qualifier (the cross-field equality the schema cannot compare; also the §16.4 discovery mechanism). (9) The Hub MUST strip submitter-side machinery before delivery: `state`, `client_ref`, and any `request.callback`/`action.callback`; `idempotency_key` is delivered (inert); the `agent` descriptor is delivered but advisory. ACK KEYS (§8.7.1): (10) `POST /v1/inbox/ack` covers all entry kinds under the pinned per-kind ack keys — directive `id`, message-entry `id`, response-entry `resolution_id`, receipt `id` — with v0.5-minted ids namespaced (`dir_`/`msg_`/`res_`/`rcpt_`; pre-0.5 ids grandfathered, the Hub remaining responsible for ack-key uniqueness across every entry it delivers); acking a foreign/unknown id is a no-op that reveals nothing. (11) Per-kind ack track effects hold: message-entry ack -> mailbox track `acknowledged`; response-entry ack == a note-less POST /v1/messages/{id}/ack under first-ack-wins; receipt ack = consume only, no track, and receipts never generate receipts. HUMAN AUDITABILITY (§8.7.1): (12) Addressed messages default out of the human triage inbox but MUST remain readable/auditable by the account's authenticated human.
